newsitem.title: USA: MCA/Viacom Delaware trial set to resume Monday.
newsitem.headline: MCA/Viacom Delaware trial set to resume Monday.

text.p: Viacom Inc and Seagram Co Ltd's MCA Inc unit are set to resume a court battle Monday over their jointly owned cable venture, USA Networks.

On Friday, after a four-day recess failed to produce a negotiated settlement, Viacom said it had withdrawn its offer which reportedly would have divided the assets to give the USA Network to Viacom and the Sci-Fi cable channel plus cash to MCA.
A source told Reuters that Seagram chief executive Edgar Bronfman Jr is expected to testify Monday.

The Delaware Chancery Court trial, which began Oct 15, was recessed for settlement talks Oct 21 after MCA had presented four of its six designated witnesses. MCA declined comment Sunday on whether it still planned to have an economics expert testify.

At issue in the trial before Vice Chancellor Myron Steele are the competing claims of MCA and Viacom about the USA joint venture. MCA witnesses have testified that Viacom's ownership of "advertiser-supported basic cable entertainment networks" outside the partnership violates the terms of the 1981 agreement.
MCA wants the court to order Viacom either to sell off its alleged competing cable interests or sell its half of the USA Networks partnership to MCA.
Viacom has said in court papers that its cable interests do not violate the agreement, and it seeks damages for MCA's alleged breach of contract and unfair competition.
The trial is expected to run for three more weeks barring any new interruptions.
Neither side would comment on why negotiations broke down or whether they would continue during the trial.
